description: Stereo overdrive modelled on a green guitar pedal, mixing a soft-clipped copy of the input back in under a lowpass tone control

params.text: Runs the signal through the overdrive when on; with it off the module is bypassed, and the switch crossfades between the two rather than stepping
Sweeps the lowpass filter on the output from a low corner up to a high one that lifts the top end; the readout runs 0 to 11
Sets the gain into the diode clipper that is mixed back with the input, so turning it up distorts more; the clipping is soft rather than hard
Sets how much of the overdriven signal is in the output against the dry input, 0 to 100% wet

inputs.text: Adds to the TONE knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DRIVE knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MIX knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the LEVEL knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
The left audio input into the overdrive
The right audio input into the overdrive

outputs.text: The left output, carrying the dry signal and the overdrive in the proportion set by MIX
The right output, carrying the dry signal and the overdrive in the proportion set by MIX

notes: the two channels are separate circuits and neither input is normalled to the other, so with nothing patched into IN II the OUT II jack stays at 0V
the circuit is modelled around a signal of ±1, and the module divides each input by 5 and multiplies each output by 5 to suit it, so ±5V is the level it expects
